The Master of Business Administration (MBA) core curriculum covers the foundation of a traditional Master of Business Administration program and includes seminars in Finance, Operations, Strategic Resource Management, Marketing, and Strategic Management. 

The program is accredited by the Accreditation Council of Business Schools and Programs (ACBSP). The mission of the ACBSP is to establish, promote, and recognize educational standards that contribute to the continuous improvement of business education and to recognize business schools that adhere to these standards.

volunteering.role: Chair- Board of Fellows- College of Graduate and Continuing
volunteering.description:
Founded in 1975, the Board of Fellows (BOF) of Norwich University is comprised of alumni and friends of Norwich University who have an abiding interest in the enrichment of the academic programs at Norwich.

The Norwich University Board of Fellows work through a variety of Visiting Committees (VC) to provide support to the several schools within the University. These committees meet at least twice a year; once during Homecoming and once in the spring. Currently there is a Visiting Committee for the following academic disciplines:

Architecture + Art
Business and Management
Engineering
Science and Mathematics
Liberal Arts
Nursing
College of Graduate and Continuing Studies
Membership on the board results from a nomination process intended to ensure that each Visiting Committee has the requisite skills. 

The Executive Committee meets several times throughout the year.

receivedRecommendations.givenAt: September 26, 2013, Cory worked with Matthew but on different teams
receivedRecommendations.description: Matt is a rock star.  There's just no other way to put it.  He is an enormously resourceful individual who excels in juggling competing priorities, anticipating (and then by-passing) problems.  Matt and I worked together in Iraq, he was Operations and I worked for the Safety department.  Prior to Matt joining the team in Ops, there was often conflict between our two teams.  Both departments had similar reporting criteria for incidents but different timetables, and it very easily morphed into a competition for information control and dissemination.  Matt changed all of that.  When he took over the Operations cell at Al Asad, he embraced transparency and fostered a culture of respect across functions.  As a result, incident reporting became a cooperative venture in which both departments worked together to accomplish their mutual objectives and satisfy contract and federal requirements.  However, his biggest achievement in Operations was introducing the necessity of a well organized, rehearsed and attainable Emergency Action Plan.  Prior to Matt's arrival, the EA Plan for our base was disjointed, incomplete and, as far as any of the base employees knew, non-existent.  Matt organized a committee of key players, pulled everyone together and coached us through the development of a solid Emergency Action procedure. He pushed this EAP initiative despite complacency and resistance among many of the employees.  As a result of his effort, training was implemented, rally points were established, accountability procedures were streamlined, and people on site had the peace of mind to know what to expect when the worst occurred.  The standards he established remained in place long after he departed Al Asad, and helped guide people through several significant incidents that come with the territory of working in a conflict zone.  He continues to be my go-to for questions on security and emergency planning, and has remained my mentor and good friend throughout the nine years I've known him.

about:
I believe that people are an organization’s most valuable asset. Diversity, equity, and inclusion are the backbone of an organizational culture that needs to be integrated into the business strategy through raising awareness and educating staff.

Throughout my career, I have dedicated efforts to fostering transformation of internal processes that would positively impact all staff members with the execution of region-wide diversity, inclusion, and equity initiatives.

As the DEI leader for EY’s fasting growing segment (government and public sector), I translate internal projects into increased revenue, sales, and partnerships. Through creating a culture of true collaboration, I have been able to align our global DEI strategy to deepen EY’s commitment to anti-racism while strengthening client relationships and supporting diverse staff members. 

My earlier experience includes management roles in IT Risk where I managed 9 out of 11 business units while overseeing a $900K budget. Even then, I championed efforts to recruit new talent and increase employee retention.

Some highlights of my career include: 

» Earned numerous awards for service excellence, including 30+ Bravo Awards, Nomination for Counselor of the Year, 2 Women Who Inspires Awards, 6 Ovation Awards and Career Impact Appreciation Award.

» Increased pipeline of minority hires by hosting EY’s First HBCU Innovation Challenge with 20+ students in partnership with 2 HBCUs that allowed students to experience a day in the life of a consultant. 

» Piloted multiple global trainings on Unconscious Bias for 40+ Senior Managers and Partners; received average satisfaction rating of 90%. 

» Launched mentoring program for Underrepresented Minorities which evolved into first Americas-wide mentoring program inclusive of all diversity dimensions; recruited 100+ mentors and ~500 mentees.

» Cultivated a diverse and inclusive organizational culture through establishing trusted alliances to develop mentoring programs, create empowering career experiences, and support diversity recruitment initiatives. 

I hold an MBA in Accounting from Hampton University and certification as a Certified Information Systems Auditor (CISA) and a SHRM-Certified Professional (SHRM-CP).

headline: Partner in Transaction Tax Advisory at EY
about: I am a Partner in the Transaction Tax Advisory practice at EY sitting in Chicago. I specialize in advising clients with respect to tax issues associated with transactions and M&A. I serve clients in all industries and sectors but have extensive experience with infrastructure and private equity investment and the broader energy sector. I have a family of 4 (one son and one daughter) and enjoy running and playing music in my spare time.

experience.description:
Matt is a Partner in the Transaction Tax Advisory practice of the International Tax and Transaction Services line at Ernst & Young LLP in Chicago, Illinois. He has almost two decades of experience in public accounting with over a decade focused entirely on transactions and M&A. He serves clients in a variety of industries including energy and infrastructure, private equity, health care, real estate and hospitality, and consumer products and heavy equipment.

Matt currently serves a variety of sponsors and corporate multinationals focusing on transaction due diligence for various entity types (e.g., partnerships, S corps, consolidated groups, CFCs, REITs, etc.), structuring and planning, legal contract review and modeling and forecasting in both domestic and cross border transactions.

Matt has advised on various transactions including leasing and concession deals, P3s, joint ventures, carve outs, take privates, IPOs and internal restructurings (including troubled debt and bankruptcy restructurings) and associated tax attribute planning (Section 382/SRLY, stock basis and E&P, purchase price allocations, etc.).

Matt has presented at TEI and other conferences on topics such as tax equity and renewable energy investment, the Inflation Reduction Act, BEPS Pillar Two, and other M&A related topics.

Prior to specializing in M&A, Matt was in the Global Compliance and Reporting practice at EY working in both DFW and Houston and had extensive experience with income tax accounting and compliance.

headline: Senior Manager, Cybersecurity, Cyber Transformation
about:
Rohit is a part of the Cybersecurity Consulting practice at EY. Rohit has a career of providing cybersecurity consulting services to fortune 100 and fortune 500 organizations in the automotive, transportation, industrial products, consumer products, healthcare and life sciences organizations. Rohit helps clients assess improvement opportunities in their cybersecurity functions, and yield high returns from subsequent investments. Rohit specializes in Cyber Program Management, Connected Product Security, Cyber Program Strategy, IT Governance and Risk Management, Vendor Risk Management, and Cyber Security Metrics.

With the future of numerous sectors moving to an increasingly connected ecosystem, there is an advancing paradigm of cyber risks ranging from intellectual property theft to connected device compromise. Rohit brings an outcome-focused approach to help clients address this broad spectrum of risks. Rohit has a demonstrated ability to innovate for his clients and provide industry leading solutions to address a wide range of risks in an increasingly connected world. 

Prior to joining EY, Rohit completed a Master’s degree in Information Systems at the Kelley School of Business, where he served as the President of the MSIS Student Association leading a team of 10. Upon graduation, Rohit was one of two winners of the MSIS Outstanding Contribution Award. Prior to that, Rohit completed an engineering degree in Information Technology. Rohit currently holds the ITIL v3 Foundation and CIPP/IT certifications. Rohit is based in Chicago, Illinois and is a frequent participant in the IT Governance, Risk and Controls course in the MSIS program at the Kelley School of Business.

projects.description:
This project was a Cloud Thought Leadership project with a team from Ernst and Young serving as clients. The core deliverable list for this project was as follows:-
1. A cloud vendor comparison model using MS Excel.
2. A cloud ROI calculation model using MS Excel.
3. A Cloud Thought Leadership white paper.
4. An executive summary of the Cloud Thought Leadership white paper.

We researched and documented one case study for each cloud deployment model (SaaS, PaaS and IaaS) for the following five industries: Financial Services, Manufacturing, Media and Entertainment, Pharmaceuticals and Healthcare.

All the deliverables were created using an iterative approach based on feedback received during weekly status calls with the client team.

about:
I am a CPA license holder and an Associate member of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Pakistan (ICAP) with a total experience of over 12 years in the field of Accounting, Finance and Audit. I am currently serving as a Manager at Ernst and Young. Previously I have also served at Palladium Group Global.

I have expertise and experience in Financial Accounting, ICS submissions, Internal Audit, External Audit, Assurance, ACR (Accounting Compliance and Reporting), Corporate Finance and Costing.

My experience has enabled me to develop a comprehensive understanding of the competitive and regulatory environments of diversified sectors, key business processes and the accounting and internal control systems implemented at various organizations while also ensuring competence in financial reporting and related matters.

I have a strong work ethic and unwavering passion for application of established knowledge; for reaping improvements and efficiencies. When tasked with responsibility, I target to achieve more than that expected of me, be it my own performance or that of my team. I am also an extremely fast learner and keep a keen eye on all the developments in the accounting and finance professions, and find research to be very invigorating.

projects.title: Mapping Land Cover from Satellite Imagery
projects.associatedWith: Associated with Metis
projects.description: A client based project for DigitalGlobe. Designed and trained a deep-learning model in Python to automatically detect, classify and map  land use from satellite imagery. Neural networks, remote sensing and GIS data analysis techniques were extensively used.

Designed and implemented MATLAB and C++ algorithms combining computer vision, image processing, machine learning and convex optimization techniques to perform pixel-level classification and segmentation of 21 classes in the Microsoft Research Cambridge dataset.

projects.title: Image Classification CIFAR-10
projects.associatedWith: Associated with Metis
projects.description: Developed a convolutional neural network based classification model using Python packages to categorize 10 classes in the CIFAR-10 dataset. Built a Flask web app that takes a test image as an input and applies the classification model to categorize the image in real time.

projects.title: Keck Spectroscopy of RGBs in dSphs of Andromeda M31
projects.associatedWith: Associated with University of California, Santa Cruz
projects.description: As a part of a broader survey of the physical properties of Local Group dwarf galaxies (dSphs), our work focused on estimating the chemical abundance[Fe/H] spread in M31 dSphs. The study was based on multi-slit spectroscopy of 100+ RGB stars observed with the Keck 10-m telescope and the Low Resolution Imaging Spectrometer, and the Hubble Space Telescope. Using model fitting and regression analysis techniques, our observational data were compared with theoretical models to gain insight into dSph formation and evolution. This project contributed to two proceedings at the American Astronomical Society Conference.

projects.title: Photometric Analysis of Field Galaxies and Galaxy Clusters at Intermediate Redshift
projects.description: At the University of California Observatories, I studied intermediate redshift galaxies. Photometric data of 25,000+ field and cluster galaxies, obtained with the Hubble Space Telescope, were analyzed to evaluate the environmental influence (field vs. cluster) on galaxy formation and evolution (nature vs. nurture). This involved image processing, classification, regression and statistical inference. The work lead to the following publication in the Astrophysical Journal.

projects.title: X-ray Luminosity Function of Low-redshift Seyfert Galaxies
projects.description: I analyzed X-ray spectra of low-redshift Seyfert galaxies observed with the Chandra X-ray Satellite. I constructed an X-ray luminosity function, which had been complementary to the existing luminosity function of Seyferts at higher redshifts. Various statistical analysis techniques and simulations based models were used to separate X-ray sources from background the luminosity estimation. My Masters thesis at Wesleyan was based on this project.

publications.title: When and How to Adopt Zero-Based Budgeting
publications.publishedAt: EPM and Business Intelligence Executive Insight · Oct 1, 2014
publications.description:
Zero-based budgeting can be an effective tool to reset the budget and planning process. While not for every
company or every situation, when there is significant change, a high level of cost pressure, or the cost structure has
become stale, ZBB helps target improvement by focusing on true cost drivers. Companies have seen sustainable
cost improvements of 25% or more by adopting this budget method. These organizations train employees to treat
every dollar of expense as if it were their own, instilling financial discipline in the organization and operating in an
environment where cost management is a way of life

publications.title: Large Global Diversified Company Retools FP&A
publications.description:
The subject of this case study is a large global manufacturer with a significant presence in numerous industries.
Over time, the company evolved and expanded both through acquisitions and organic growth. This led to the
adoption of a decentralized management approach to its hundreds of operating companies in dozens of countries.
While advantageous in many respects, this model increased the finance organization’s operating costs, particularly
in providing FP&A services. To address the issue, finance embarked on a planning-process transformation initiative
designed to improve efficiency and reduce cost while boosting service levels. Within the first year of the initiative,
over 60% of internal survey respondents rated the target-setting process as “better” or “significantly better” than in
prior years. Further, some business units successfully adopted the best practice of linked planning events, saving major
amounts of time and eliminating unnecessary work

publications.title: Rolling Forecasts: Why They So Often End in Failure, and How to Avoid This Fate

headline: Senior Manager | Enterprise Platform & Engineering Leader | Microsoft Power Platform, Dynamics, Architecture
about:
I began my career as a software developer, building enterprise applications and steadily taking on greater technical and leadership responsibility. Over nearly 11 years at Houghton Mifflin Harcourt’s Riverside Publishing division, I progressed from developer to Director of Software Product Development, leading client-facing, subscription-based platforms and managing distributed teams of up to 25 engineers, analysts, and Scrum Masters. During this time, I focused on scaling both technology and teams, modernizing delivery practices, and mentoring leaders as the organization grew.

After establishing a strong foundation in enterprise product development and people leadership, I moved into consulting to broaden my exposure across industries and delivery models. At Sonoma Partners, I served as a Principal Developer, where I combined hands-on technical leadership with architecture, delivery ownership, and client advisory. I led enterprise CRM implementations across Microsoft Dynamics and Salesforce, coached developers, contributed to recruiting and pre-sales, and partnered directly with client leadership to shape solution strategy.

That experience set the stage for my transition to EY Consulting, where I applied the same core strengths, technical depth, delivery leadership, and client partnership at significantly greater scale. At EY, I led Microsoft Power Platform and Dynamics implementations for large, complex organizations, guiding multi-disciplinary teams, mentoring leaders, and owning client outcomes within highly regulated, enterprise environments.

Across each stage of my career, the common thread has been building strong teams, translating business needs into pragmatic, well architected solutions, and maintaining a deep connection to the technology while taking on progressively broader leadership responsibility.

experience.position: EY Consulting Senior Manager – Microsoft Power Platform & Dynamics
experience.description:
I joined EY Consulting as a Manager and was promoted to Senior Manager after two years, reflecting expanded responsibility across delivery leadership, people management, and client outcomes. In this role, I lead Microsoft Power Platform and Dynamics implementations for large, highly regulated enterprise clients.

I am responsible for end-to-end delivery across multiple engagements, including technical strategy, architectural direction, and execution. This includes leading multi-disciplinary, geographically distributed teams, ensuring alignment with enterprise governance, security, and compliance standards; and guiding programs from initiation through deployment.

As my scope expands, I move beyond program level leadership into broader portfolio and capability ownership, mentoring managers and senior consultants, shaping delivery standards and best practices, and contributing to the growth of Power Platform and Dynamics capabilities within the firm. I also support business development by advising clients on platform strategy, shaping solution approaches, and contributing to proposals and pursuit efforts.

This role represents a deliberate progression from hands-on technical leadership into enterprise scale delivery and organizational influence, while remaining closely connected to the technology and the teams executing it.

I joined Sonoma Partners to broaden my impact beyond a single product organization and apply my technical leadership across multiple industries and delivery models. As a Principal Developer, I served as the senior technical lead for enterprise CRM implementations across Microsoft Dynamics CRM and Salesforce, supporting clients in insurance, retail, manufacturing, publishing, and financial services.

In this role, I owned the technical direction and delivery of projects end to end, leading architecture and design decisions, validating solution approaches, providing delivery estimates, and ensuring quality through code reviews and hands-on guidance. I partnered directly with client leadership as a trusted technical advisor, facilitating design sessions, leading technical presentations, and translating complex business needs into pragmatic, scalable solutions.

My responsibilities extended beyond project delivery into organizational leadership. I coached and mentored developers at all experience levels, contributed to recruiting through interviews and candidate evaluation, and supported internal capability development. I also played an active role in pre-sales efforts, providing architectural input and helping shape solution strategies during the sales process.

This role allowed me to deepen my architectural and client advisory skills while leading multiple teams and engagements, setting the foundation for operating at enterprise scale.

I joined Riverside Publishing as a software developer and progressed through a series of increasingly senior roles including Senior Developer, Architect, Team Lead, and Development Manager ultimately becoming Director of Software Product Development. Over nearly 11 years, I was responsible for the end-to-end development, delivery, and support of client-facing, subscription based online products.

As Director, I led local and distributed teams of up to 25 software developers, business analysts, and Scrum Masters, overseeing both day-to-day delivery and longer-term product and platform strategy. I partnered closely with internal stakeholders and external clients to translate business and user needs into scalable, reliable solutions, ensuring delivery was both timely and cost effective.

A core focus of my leadership was modernizing development practices. I helped integrate Agile methodologies into a structured SDLC, improving transparency, predictability, and collaboration while continuing to meet demanding business and client expectations. Throughout my tenure, I maintained a hands-on mindset, staying close to the code when needed and fostering open dialogue between engineering, product, and clients to maximize team effectiveness.

Equally important was people development. I coached and mentored developers at all skill levels, and later supported and mentored managers as they grew into leadership roles themselves, building a strong, sustainable development organization.

As a Software Developer at marchFirst, I worked on client facing software implementations, contributing to the design, development, testing, and deployment of custom solutions based on detailed business and technical requirements. I collaborated closely with project team members to deliver features and enhancements aligned with project plans, priorities, and timelines.

My responsibilities included implementing and testing application modules, documenting technical designs, and supporting analysis efforts for new and upgraded systems. This role provided a strong foundation in professional software development practices, client delivery, and working within structured project environments.

As a Web Developer at AANA, I supported a broad range of IT and application needs in a small team environment, gaining hands-on experience across infrastructure, support, and software development. I worked directly with internal users to address both day-to-day technical issues and longer term application needs.

My responsibilities included maintaining and updating the organization’s public website and member self-service web application, supporting internal servers through routine maintenance and updates, and contributing to the design and development of internal business applications used across multiple departments. I also developed data driven solutions, including Microsoft Access applications connected to enterprise data sources, to improve reporting and usability for business users.

This role provided early exposure to full-stack problem solving, user-facing systems, and the operational side of IT, building a strong foundation for later work in enterprise software development and technical leadership.

headline: Assistant Director of Global Innovation Marketing at EY | Named Among Five Outstanding Young Dallasites | IABC Gold Quill Award | City of Dallas Pride in Excellence Civic Engagement Award | Community volunteer
about:
I am a marketing practitioner passionate about innovation, inclusion, and social impact. At EY, I manage communications and sponsorships for the global innovation program and advanced tech labs, including AI and Quantum.

Professional Background:
With a diverse career, I have held marketing and business development positions at Deloitte, BlackBerry, and Baker Botts as well as higher education administration positions at SMU and Kansas State University. My expertise lies in leading strategic programs and fostering stakeholder collaboration. I served on the Board of Governors at the Human Rights Campaign and earned a master's degree in college student development and counseling. My civic engagement includes serving as a planning and zoning commissioner for Dallas, focusing on sustainable design, housing affordability, and equity.

Presentations:

-Impact of Corporate Employee Pride and LGBTQ+ Engagement Programs: World Affairs Council of Dallas/Ft Worth

Awards:

-Marketing Awards: IABC Gold Quill Award, ANA Marketing Activation Award Finalist, Hermes Creative Awards Gold and Platinum, AVA International Digital Awards Platinum, SABRE Awards North America Finalist, North America Excellence Award for Multi-Channel Communications

headline: EY Partner, Tax Accounting and Risk Advisory Services | Qualified Financial Expert | Global Business Leader | Board & C-Suite Advisor
about:
As a certified financial accounting expert with extensive experience in guiding organizations through strategic transactions, technology-enabled transformations, and diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI) initiatives, I am passionate about creating long-term value for businesses.

In my role as a senior partner at EY, a global leader in professional services with a footprint in 150 countries, I have successfully managed multimillion-dollar tax accounting practices, serving clients ranging from startups to multinational corporations. My deep operational and client service experience allows me to act as a trusted advisor to boards and C-suite executives, helping them explore the “art of the possible” to drive efficiencies and optimize value.
A few highlights of my career include:

•	Global Operating Leadership: I led EY’s multimillion-dollar Americas Tax Accounting Managed Service practice, overseeing a large team of professionals across 30 countries, where I implemented innovative operations strategies that achieved annual revenue growth of up to 20%, while advising several of the firm’s highest profile clients.

•	Transaction Expertise: My extensive experience in pre-IPO tax planning and transaction management has enabled companies to navigate complex tax implications associated with acquisitions, IPOs, and other strategic initiatives.

•	Transformative Solutions: As EY’s Global Tax Smart Delivery Leader, I spearheaded one of the firm’s largest transformation initiatives, effectively integrating people, processes, and technology to enhance service delivery and streamline tax provision processes.

•	Governance and DEI Champion: I serve on the Advisory Board for the Paton School at the University of Michigan, providing insights on governance and financial matters. A passionate advocate for DEI, I co-founded Chicago’s Pan-Asian professional network and actively engage with Fortune 100 companies to advance inclusive practices in the workplace.

•	Thought Leader: I regularly speak at industry conferences and have co-authored publications on emerging tax issues. My commitment to advancing diversity earned me the Outstanding Leadership in Advancing Diversity Award from the Illinois CPA Society.

I believe in the power of collaboration and innovation to drive transformative change. I welcome the opportunity to connect to explore opportunities for growth and impact.

Industry Experience: Financial Services | Consumer Products | Automotive | Industrial Products | Medical Products | Private Equity | Technology

experience.description: Throughout my career with EY, I’ve held several prominent leadership roles, including leading the Tax Accounting and Risk Advisory Services annuity team, serving as the Americas Tax Accounting Annuity Center Leader and the EY Global Tax Accounting and Risk Advisory Services C2 Provision Tax Smart Delivery Program Leader. In each of these roles, I’ve worked with international teams to build enablers and processes needed to support the standardization, automation and centralization of the delivery of provisioning. slides.title: Achieving Virtual Success
slides.subtitle: Timothy Le on LinkedIn
slides.description:
As a result of the COVID-19 pandemic, the education system had to revitalize their programs in order to respond appropriately. As a current junior of Indiana University, I was confused about how we would be able to continue high quality education while implementing new protocols to address the pandemic. However, here at Indiana University, we were able to overcome the pandemic and provide quality education. Here are some tips I have implemented to achieve virtual success. Develop an Agenda

 While this first step may seem obvious, it is often ignored, especially in small group meetings for projects or presentations. An important skill to develop is the ability to create a detailed agenda with an approximate time estimate for each activity so your team can generate an idea of what to expect from the meeting. This will result in a smoother meeting with less questions along with a framework team members can reference later on. I was able to implement this skill throughout my Compass III class by arranging a meeting, developing an agenda, and leading that meeting. Break Intervals

 An important skill I adopted as a student is the ability to take a break. Often times, individuals can get "burned" out by being online for too long. As a result, these individuals find their motivation to be lower and their quality of work to be less than their standard. To combat this issue, implement break intervals! Take a 5-15 minute break every hour and every few hours, take a full break to do something meaningful, such as making a meal, exercising, catching up with friends and family, or anything you find meaningful! I have implemented this skill in my life and have felt much less stress and increased productivity. Feedback

 Giving and Receiving Feedback was one of our modules within Compass III that resonated deeply with me. Often times, people underestimate how effective feedback can be. We learned a new acronym to assist us in receiving feedback: AWARE. A - Ask for feedback W - Watch your emotions A - Ask questions to clarify R - Reach out for different perspectives E - Engage your potential With this acronym, we can better understand feedback and turn the feedback process into actionable steps. Concluding Thoughts

 As I grow as a leader, I will take these various tips to propel my virtual success in both the classroom and outside. The world is perpetually evolving through innovations and global changes, and it is important for us to adapt to these changes in order to succeed. While in-person interactions may be limited at the moment, we are still able to grow our network and develop ourselves.

publications.title: Latest Stock Buyback Tax Rules May Still Have Wide Reach
publications.description:
Eversheds Sutherland attorneys Xenia Garofalo and Kyle Colonna are quoted in this Law360 article discussing the proposed regulations that the U.S. Treasury Department recently issued for the stock buyback excise tax.
 
Specifically, Xenia and Kyle addressed if there is a risk that the funding rule in the proposed regulations could characterize avoidance in a way that would trigger the excise tax for routine intercompany transactions.
 
“A best practice going forward is maintaining sufficient documentation supporting the reasons for undertaking intercompany transactions,” the two said. 
 
Routine intercompany transactions entered into for valid business reasons would not be problematic, particularly if they have been historically undertaken by the company prior to the issuance of the notice and the proposed regulations, according to an email from the two attorneys. However, "a principal purpose" is an amorphous standard, they said.
 
"Taxpayers need [to pay] close attention to their intercompany transactions to ensure that a seemingly innocent routine intercompany transaction cannot otherwise be interpreted by the IRS as entered into with a principal purpose of avoiding the stock buyback tax," Xenia and Kyle added.

On March 9, the White House released President Joe Biden's proposed budget for fiscal year 2024, and in connection therewith, the US Department of the Treasury released "General Explanations of the Administration's Fiscal Year 2024 Revenue Proposals," also called the Green Book.

In general, the Green Book sets forth and explains the Biden administration's revenue proposals, describes the existing tax laws that the proposals would affect and provides reasoning in support of any changes to such tax laws.

In this article published by Law360, Eversheds Sutherland attorneys Xenia Garofalo and Kyle Colonna discuss the significant changes to tax laws in the administration's budget proposal, and why multinational corporations should be proactive by evaluating the potential impact of the proposals.

publications.title: Unpacking The Interim Guidance On New Stock Buyback Tax
publications.description: On December 27, 2022, Treasury and the IRS released Notice 2023-2, announcing their intent to issue proposed regulations addressing the application of the new excise tax on repurchases of corporate stock under section 4501, which takes effect on January 1, 2023. The Notice provides taxpayers with interim guidance that Treasury and the IRS expect to be consistent with the forthcoming proposed regulations. Until issuance of the proposed regulations, taxpayers may rely on section 3 of the Notice. The Interim Guidance addresses, inter alia, calculation of the Buyback Tax and its application to reorganizations, spin-offs, liquidations, certain stock exchanges, stock issuances to employees, as well as other routine corporate transactions.

publications.description: When advising clients on cross-border transactions, whether the client will qualify for treaty benefits is often an issue that needs to be addressed. This panel will provide a guide to how to analyze a U.S. tax treaty and will address some of the common withholding tax provisions, when and how business profits are taxed, and whether a person will qualify for treaty benefits under the limitation on benefits clause. The panel will also provide an overview of typical transactions in which treaty benefits may be applicable, how transactions are structured to provide for treaty benefits, and how treaty disputes are resolved.

publications.title: Next Stop on the corporate minimum tax train: Issues which require guidance
publications.description: Nearly two months ago, on August 16, 2022, President Biden signed the Inflation Reduction Act of 2022 (the IRA) into law. Among the most notable IRA provisions is a 15% corporate alternative minimum tax on corporations with book profits exceeding $1 billion (the CMT). For previous reporting by Eversheds Sutherland regarding the CMT, see Signed, sealed, delivered: Biden signs Inflation Reduction Act enacting “new” corporate minimum tax and Back from the dead: Corporate minimum tax resurfaces at eleventh hour in Inflation Reduction Act of 2022. The CMT is effective for taxable years beginning after December 31, 2022. As a result, taxpayers are working to understand whether they are liable for the CMT, and, if so, to what extent. Inevitably, this analysis has resulted in the identification of a number of areas for which immediate guidance is necessary. As we await implementation and clarifying guidance from the IRS and Treasury, this alert highlights a number of preliminary issues relating to the CMT for which guidance is appropriate.

publications.title: Unpacking The New Stock Buyback Tax And Its Exceptions
Inflation Reduction Act imposes a nondeductible 1% excise tax on certain corporate stock buybacks
publications.description: On August 16, 2022, President Biden signed the Inflation Reduction Act of 2022 (the IRA) into law. Among the provisions of the IRA is a nondeductible 1% excise tax on the repurchase of corporate stock (the Buyback Tax). The Buyback Tax is directly levied on repurchasing corporations, which means that corporations that currently have, or are considering, the adoption of stock buyback programs will need to include the Buyback Tax in the evaluation of the costs of any such program. Not all stock buybacks are covered by the tax, and there are a number of exceptions that may apply to limit the impact of the Buyback Tax, as discussed in more detail below. The Buyback Tax is effective for transactions occurring in taxable years after December 31, 2022.

publications.title: Signed, sealed, delivered: Biden signs Inflation Reduction Act enacting “new” corporate minimum tax
publications.description: On August 16, 2022, President Biden signed the Inflation Reduction Act of 2022 (the IRA) into law. Among the most notable IRA provisions is a 15% corporate alternative minimum tax on corporations with book profits exceeding $1 billion effective for taxable years beginning after December 31, 2022 (the AMT). Originally a provision of the now-defunct Build Back Better Act, the AMT was revived by Senators Chuck Schumer and Joe Manchin earlier this month. The AMT managed to survive the budget reconciliation process, including a “vote-a-rama” in the Senate (i.e., a procedure in which Senators propose an unlimited amount of amendments to budget-related bills). The corporate AMT applies only if the 15% rate applied to a designated corporation’s financial statement income exceeding $1 billion with adjustments is greater than the corporation’s regular US Federal income tax liability plus any base erosion anti-abuse tax (BEAT). According to the Joint Committee on Taxation, approximately 150 of the world’s largest companies may potentially be subject to the AMT.1 Consequently, there are a range of issues to consider in applying this new tax.

publications.title: Multinational Corporations After Tax Reform: Converting Non-Intercompany Obligations into Intercompany Obligations
Applying the rescission doctrine to dividend distributions: A practical guide
publications.description:
Dividends — the primary means by which corporations transfer after-tax earnings to shareholders — are used in a variety of contexts. Some contexts are routine, such as quarterly dividend distributions, while other contexts are targeted to achieve a specific corporate purpose. In the targeted context, planning often is a dynamic process.
As planning and circumstances evolve, already consummated transactions may not survive as part of the plan; in that case, the legal concept of rescission may be available as an integral planning tool. Rescission, nonetheless, has its limits, particularly for legally declared dividends. Attempting to unwind a legally declared dividend without the appropriate planning is a trap for the unwary. Accordingly, this discussion explores the rescission doctrine, in general and in the dividend context, and provides insight into potential planning opportunities to avoid the trap of unwinding a dividend.

publications.title: The Three Ds: D, Dover, and Directionality
publications.publishedAt: TAXES - The Tax Magazine® / CCH · Feb 1, 2018
publications.description: This column presents two “check and sell” transactions, each of which involves an election by a subsidiary corporation to change its status to disregarded followed by a sale of such subsidiary to a related corporation. Subsequently, this column addresses the “check-the-box regulations,” “D” reorganizations, Dover, “C” reorganizations, and post-reorganization asset transfers under Code Sec. 368(a)(2)(C) and Reg. §1.368-2(k). In doing so, this column examines the potential U.S. federal income tax consequences of the two previously mentioned scenarios, compares the consequences of the potential characterizations of Scenario 2, and explores the implications of Scenario 2 in the cross-border context in an attempt to illustrate the uncertainty imposed by the three-Ds: D, Dover, and Directionality.

publications.title: Autonomous Cars and Tort Liability
publications.publishedAt: 4 Case W. Res. J. L. Tech. & Internet 1 (2012)
publications.description: With the passing of time, cars are becoming more autonomous and independent of human intervention. However, with this shift in control from humans to technology, there also comes a shift in liability. While autonomous cars will eliminate many accidents caused by human error, many others will result due to technological malfunctions. In order to ensure that autonomous cars enter the marketplace in a timely fashion, the liability of autonomous car manufacturers requires mitigation. This Note examines the legal issues surrounding autonomous cars, including tort liability, and proposes a means by which the liability issues surrounding autonomous cars may be fashioned in order to effectuate a timely implementation of autonomous cars in the marketplace.

publications.title: Recognizing the Importance of Intrabrand Competition in High-Technology Markets: The Problem With Large Retailers & Vertical Territorial Restraints
publications.publishedAt: 4 Case W. Res. J. L. Tech. & Internet 2 (2013)
publications.description: High technology markets are unique, particularly because they innovate at a significantly faster pace than other markets. Due to the increasing complexity of the technology products sold, consumers require adequate customer service in order to form informed decisions with respect to purchases. Current antitrust laws provide for special treatment regarding interbrand competition. However, an increase in interbrand competition may result in a decrease in intrabrand competition. The detrimental effect of a decrease in intrabrand competition is evident when vertical territorial restraints are imposed on large retailers that are lacking in the customer service department. Courts are lacking in uniformity and guidance regarding vertical territorial restraints and the application of the rule of reason. The Supreme Court provided some guidance in "Board of Trade of City of Chicago v. United States", but much of that guidance has gone all but unheeded. As a result, this Comment proposes a three-prong test to assist in defining the "peculiarity factor" set forth by the Supreme Court.

headline: Delivering Development Solutions: Real Estate, Economic Growth, and Incentive Programs
about:
Jennifer is an experienced real estate development professional focusing on all aspects of pre-development planning including site diligence, zoning and entitlements, and credits and incentives.  She is part of EY’s Global Location Investment Services- Credits & Incentives Advisory Practice.  She serves as the Tax Increment Financing (TIF) subject matter lead for EY US and is the State Desk Credits & Incentives leader for North Carolina and South Carolina and Illinois resource for domestic and global inbound investment. 

She acts as a trusted advisor with real estate developers, private corporations, state and local governments and economic development officials on matters related to real estate development and business investment and expansion to secure local, state and federal statutory and discretionary incentives.  Jennifer has lead engagements in the Carolinas, Illinois, and Midwest, aligning private-sector real estate development and business investments with state and local legislative frameworks and economic priorities. 

A proven deal maker, Jennifer has over 25 years of success in working with all aspects of TIF, land acquisition, zoning and entitlements, planning, deal structuring, redevelopment agreement negotiation, early-stage project management, and creative approaches to capital and public-private project evaluation and funding.  She has particular depth in multifamily housing and mixed-use development, assisting in the development of thousands of new infill rental and for sale units, and the repositioning of underperforming shopping center properties to accommodate market-supported mixed-use development programs.  

Jennifer is also actively engaged in assisting companies identify the credit and incentive opportunities available under the Inflation Reduction Act of 2022 as well as providing compliance services to assist companies in the realization and maintenance of the credits.

experience.description:
Jennifer is part of EY’s Global Location Investment Services- Credits & Incentives Advisory Practice.  She works with private corporations, state and local governments and economic development officials on matters related to real estate development and statutory and discretionary incentives. She is actively engaged in assisting clients navigate, identify and align capital investment projects with the credit and incentive opportunities available under the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (IIJA), Inflation Reduction Act (IRA) and CHIPS Act of 2022.

A proven deal maker, Jennifer has over 20 years of success in working with developers, property owners, municipalities, and quasi-public agencies on all aspects of tax increment financing (TIF), zoning and entitlements, planning, deal structuring, redevelopment agreement negotiation, early-stage project management, and creative approaches to capital and public-private project evaluation and funding.   

Jennifer has prepared financial analysis and negotiation services to secure the approval new real estate development and redevelopment projects and business retention together with leverage from federal, state and local credit and incentives throughout the US central region.  In addition, she has assisted dozens of clients with economic development projects and initiatives throughout the US including new incentive district designations, negotiated incentives, feasibility analyses, and special studies.

Jennifer is a recognized subject matter professional on state and local economic incentives qualification, structuring, and negotiation including tax increment financing (TIF) as well as other programs.  She has spoken to various groups including the Institute for Professionals in Taxation (IPT), Illinois Tax Increment Association (ITIA), the International Council of Shopping Centers (ICSC), the Council of Development Finance Agencies (CDFA), and Stanford University’s Graduate School of Engineering.

Jennifer has nearly 20 years of progressive experience and success within the real estate development and municipal consulting field.  In this role, Jennifer served as the municipal TIF consultant for the Bell Works redevelopment, a transformational, 150-acre project that includes the former AT&T headquarters located north of Interstate 90 in Hoffman Estates, IL.

Jennifer joined Ehlers in 2014 as a Municipal Advisor and Principal of the Illinois office.  She worked with municipalities on all aspects of TIF consulting, development feasibility and pro forma analysis, public revenue projections, incentive negotiation, and creative approaches to capital and public-private project evaluation and funding.  Highlights include:
•   Managed a team of eight professionals providing municipal advisory and economic development-related services to over 100 municipal clients in northern Illinois.  Responsible for team compliance with all applicable MSRB rules and regulations.
•   Served as one of five Principals responsible for the company’s general operations as overseen by the President.
•   Lead advisor to Illinois municipalities on TIF and incentive analysis, real estate economics, proforma analysis and bond feasibility.
•   Strategic negotiator of financial and business terms of Redevelopment Agreements, Economic Incentive Agreements, municipal securities, and other deal structures.

Prior to joining Ehlers, Jennifer formed and worked for her own firm, THE TAMMEN GROUP where she represented both public and private sector entities on matters related to zoning and entitlements, planning, economic development, TIF, deal structuring, and project management.

The Tammen Group is a professional services firm specializing in real estate development strategies and solutions; economic and financial analysis; and community relations and public affairs consulting.  Jennifer's strong analytical skills and positive working relationships with municipalities and the private sector resulted in the approval of nearly $1 billion in new real estate development projects and business retention and more than $75 million in TIF and other financial subsidies in the Chicagoland market. Jennifer has been a key team member on a number of projects including TIF eligibility studies, financial feasibility and modeling, and redevelopment planning.  Jennifer is also an experienced meeting facilitator and has successfully led dozens of community meetings and presentations in addition to hundreds of meetings with clients, municipal and agency officials and staff, community residents, businesses, and other stakeholders. She served as the Economic Development Consultant for the City of Des Plaines and as a Planning Project Manager for the Public Building Commission of Chicago.

Areas of service and expertise include:
DEVELOPMENT SERVICES: TAX INCREMENT FINANCING (TIF), ECONOMIC INCENTIVES & ENTITLEMENTS
o TIF and Business District creation and designation 
o Financial feasibility analysis
o Public revenues projections
o Development Agreement evaluation and structuring
o Project review and identification of potential sources of funding 
PUBLIC AGENCY ADVOCACY & MANAGEMENT
o Coordinate government relations activities for legislative, quasi-judicial, and administrative actions
o Prepare submittal packages for RFQ’s, RFP’s and project applications
o Negotiate project concessions and mitigations with agency staff including renegotiations for stalled or existing projects 
o Public hearing management

publications.title: Czy wyrok TSUE w sprawie Schrems II jeszcze bardziej przyspieszy powstanie „polskiej chmury”?
publications.description: Sytuacja pandemii Covid-19, zamknięcie całych sektorów gospodarki, przeniesienie pracy do trybu zdalnego i paląca konieczność uelastycznienia prowadzonego biznesu pokazały, że jedną z kluczowych technologii dla przetrwania w tych trudnych czasach jest szeroko rozumiana technologia chmurowa. Dla prawnika jednak chmura obliczeniowa to przede wszystkim przetwarzanie danych osobowych. Przy korzystaniu z usług chmurowych kluczowe jest zapewnienie odpowiedniego poziomu ochrony danych osobowych, które będą przekazywane i przetwarzane u dostawcy chmurowego. Ponieważ najwięksi dostawcy chmurowi często korzystają z centrów danych zlokalizowanych poza EOG, w tym przede wszystkim w Stanach Zjednoczonych, warto zastanowić się, jaki wpływ na przetwarzanie danych w chmurze będzie miał nowy wyrok Trybunału Sprawiedliwości Unii Europejskiej z 16 lipca 2020 roku w sprawie Schrems II? Czy wyrok przełoży się na inwestycje w centra danych w Europie i Polsce?

publications.title: Chmura w sektorze ubezpieczeniowym
publications.description: Pandemia COVID–19 pokazała, że technologia chmury obliczeniowej jest kluczowa dla utrzymania ciągłości działania organizacji. Wdrożenie rozwiązań chmurowych zwiększa elastyczność biznesową i przyspiesza tempo zmian we wszystkich branżach na całym świecie. Jakie regulacje wyznaczają kierunki działania dla pełnego procesu wdrożenia chmury w sektorze ubezpieczeniowym? Zapraszam wraz z Justyna Wilczyńska-Baraniak do lektury naszego artykułu w Miesięcznik Ubezpieczeniowy

publications.title: Current Trends in Banking Technology Regulations
publications.description:
Maciej Gawroński and Joanna Galajda, lawyers from the Digital team in Bird & Bird Warsaw office, have co-authored the chapter, "Current Trends in Banking Technology Regulations"​ in the book "Challenges Facing Banking IT"​, published by the Gdansk Academy of Banking. Maciej Gawroński also co-authored the chapter, "Time for a Cloud in the Financial Sector in Poland!"​. The publication was prepared by a diverse group of IT and financial market specialists, and was edited by Andrzej Kawiński and Andrzej Sieradz for the 2015 European Financial Congress.

"Challenges Facing Banking IT 2015"​ is a continuation of the Gdansk Academy of Banking publication of the same title in 2014. The book discusses technology in the finance sector, specifically current challenges and potential problems which will be faced in the coming years by financial institutions in Poland. Readers will acquire basic knowledge of mobile banking, cloud computing, transaction security and the multi-channel distribution of financial products and services. The publication also contains the authors'​ recommendations on key issues concerning the development of products and services in the modern financial sector, particularly banking services performed through the use of mobile technologies.

The chapters prepared by experts from Bird & Bird's Warsaw office mainly relate to the legal aspects of cloud computing in the banking sector. They give recommendations on how to regulate outsourcing in the financial sector, to help banks with extensive use of cloud solutions. The authors also reviewed the updated Polish and EU regulations in the field of personal data protection and addressed issues related to legal regulation of cybersecurity in Poland and abroad.

about:
As Manager of AI & Data at EY, I collaborate on leveraging predictive modeling and building scalable data pipelines to support strategic business decisions. My work focuses on developing impactful data-driven transformations and enabling marketing initiatives through advanced analytics and teamwork.  

With a Master of Science in Business Analytics from the University of Illinois at Chicago and a Bachelor’s in Electrical and Electronics Engineering from Sikkim Manipal Institute of Technology, I combine academic knowledge with practical expertise. My goal is to drive scalable analytical solutions that deliver strategic insights and enhance organizational outcomes.

profileTopEducation.schoolName: University of Illinois at Chicago (UIC) - Liautaud Graduate School of Business

experience.description:
• Customer acquisition and valuations: Developed and commercialized insights from a regression model to over 160+ Credit Unions, that informs the best leads to target for Wealth Management products, combined with their Net-value.
• Built a Convolutional Neural Net model to predict the Net Liquid Assets and Upside opportunity of customers, enabling expansion strategies that generated additional Asset Under Management and revenue.

•Lead Predictor for Wealth Management products: Developed and commercialized a predictive model using Logistic regression with 85% accuracy, that generates propensity scores for Credit Union (CU) members based on their likelihood to buy CMFG financial products. Email campaign ran for the Top 20% leads from the model fared with an Open Rate of 27%, compared to an industry average of 21%. The model also helps identify the Top member persona segments and their geolocation, that drives Target Market Campaigning for CUs.
 •Advisor Book of Business Optimization: Spearheaded the development of a recommender engine for wealth management customers, along with a scoring model custom-made for financial advisors, aimed at prioritizing targets between associate and lead advisors. The pilot phase has shown a 5 point increase in Share of Wallet based on Asset Under Management for a sample of the group.
 • Territory Optimization: Used spatial analytics to optimize Financial Advisor coverage around branches of a Credit Union based on current and potential customer-base, reducing travel costs by prioritizing Branches with highest opportunity in terms of Net-Income.

•Tweet Analysis: Created an end to end framework to provide real time client engagement strategies to Sales teams by discovering the most popular topics on Twitter and their general sentiment across different client segments using Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) and Lexicon Analysis respectively.
•Customer Segmentation: Performed segmentation of clients to create data driven sales territories to align the right resources with the right clients. The clients were also ranked based on features like scalability, sustainability, profitability and revenue opportunity to provide sales teams with prioritized target list.

headline: Managing Director at EY
about:
SUMMARY       
	Managing Director with EY's Transformation Design & Execution practice.  12 years of experience helping our client transform their business through designing, setting-up and executing program management offices.
	Partner with Accenture’s System Integration & Technology SAP practice. Twenty-one years experience in Business and Technology Consulting with demonstrated success at Fortune 100 and 500 companies. 
	Proven ability to manage large-scale, complex programs to deliver measurable results and achieve strategic objectives. Extensive experience with the full system development life cycle for packaged and custom system implementations.
	Responsible for managing budgets up to $100M as well as managing large diverse teams of up to 700 resources.
	Consistently held leadership roles of increasing responsibility on both Process and Project Management teams.  Responsible for leadership tasks ranging from developing direct reports to delivering Project Steering Committee briefings.  Demonstrated ability to drive decision making and develop strong working relationships with C-level executives. 
	Experienced in managing various delivery models leveraging both on-shore and off-shore development teams.
	Negotiated Statements of Work to confirm contractual obligations. Experienced in managing sub-contractor and vendor relationships.
	Consulted as a program/project management subject matter expert and/or quality assurance executive.  Collaborated with senior executives to provide strategic direction and review proposed approaches for ERP implementations.
	Demonstrated experience in driving a complete sales cycle for both middle market and large scale ERP implementations.
	Demonstrated experience in driving software delivery following a rigorous methodology.
	Viewed as an outstanding people developer.  Creates a trust-based relationship with people, listens to them, advises them, showing genuine interest, respect and understanding of their personal constraints and preferences.

Specialties: Large Scale Program Management (400+ team members), Project Management, SAP Implementations, Budget Management, Contract Management, Consulting Sales

experience.description:
Responsible for leading sales opportunities within the SI&T - SAP Practice.  Managed estimating of work, pricing, client visits, and presentations for various opportunities.
Highlights of responsibilities include: 
* Managing overall project solutioning and estimating of the work effort
* Managing price to win and margin analysis
* Managing overall proposal effort including the written response, preparation for client presentations, executing client presentations, and responding to follow up questions

Responsible for managing over 200,000 work days that were executed by approximately 500 core team members and approximately 300 implementation team members.  The program was a key strategic initiative supporting Accenture CIO's Finance Transformation Program.  Scope included all 46 countries in which Accenture operates.

Highlights of responsibilities include:
* Designing, standardizing, and implementing program processes including: Scope Management, Risk Management, Issue Management, Resource Management, and Financial Management
* Implementing Earned Value Analysis across the project team to aid tracking and managing the overall progress of the program
* Managing overall program tools including: Microsoft Project 2000, a Web-Based portal for resource management, and deliverable tracking and management via a Lotus Notes database.
* Managing a decentralized team.

Responsible for initial program solution, estimating, and pricing for a multi-release, multi-year program.  Once sold, was responsible for setting up the Program Management Office for the initial $180M effort.
Highlights of responsibilities include: 
* Implementing a global PMO office for a large, global, multi-year transformation and SAP Implementation project
* Designing, implementing, and standardizing many processes for the program including: Scope Management, Issue Management, Risk Management, Resource Management, and Financial Management
* Implementing tools that included: an Integrated Milestone & Dependency plan, a standard weekly scorecard and status report, and timetracking.  The information was gathered and utilized by program and project leadership on a weekly basis.
* Designing, implementing, and managing the overall program tools including: Microsoft Project Server, Sharepoint Team Services, SAP Solution Manager, and the Rational Tools Suite.

Responsible for leading delivery of the solution for PepsiCo's SAP implementation.  Managed strategic planning, design, build, test and rollout phases for an SAP Implementation program of $1.3B.
Highlights of responsibilities include:
* Managing four concurrent releases with an additional two releases in the planning stage
* Managing over 700 core team members across multiple work locations including Chicago; Managing $100M+  annual revenue
* Managing Finance, Operations, Human Resources, Resource Sourcing (offshore)and the Commercial Negotiations for the overall program.
* Managing the Program Management Office whose responsibilities included:
* Designing, implementing, managing standard management processes for the program team
* Creating and managing resource level loaded work plans for each project team
* Preparing and analyzing weekly status reporting included EVA to the project CFO, CIO and Business Sponsors
* Managing and administering the program management tool suite.

Project Management Roles - SAP Implementations
Led several teams through various phases of SAP Implementations including

* Responsible for managing overall implementation of a mid-market client.  Responsibilities included: managing overall budget and work days, process design, configuration, development, system testing, training design and delivery, and deployment.
* Data Warehouse Lead:  Managed custom data warehouse team for a large SAP Implementation in the Semi-Conductor industry.  Managed the design of the data marts and reports required to support the implementation.  Managed the production support team for six-months after go-live
* Process Architect: Managed the integrated design for an SAP implementation.  Responsible for overall work plan, and budget.  In addition, was responsible for ensuring the overall design was integrated and efficient across all SAP modules.
* Development Lead: Responsible for managing the development for SAP implementation.  Managed the overall priority of completing the development objects while completing within budget.
* Order to Cash Lead: Managed overall SAP Order to Cash design.  Responsible for design, configuration, unit testing, system testing, and training documentation and delivery for start up business.
Process Re-engineering Lead
Supported several clients in reengineering their business processes.  Focused on Order to Cash and Request to Delivery business processes. Responsible for understanding the as-is process and defining the to-be processes.  The to-be processes were inputs into SAP Implementation Projects.

Team Lead
Led several project teams in various phases of packaged implementation projects including: design, implementation, and training of the procure to payment processes and the order to cash processes.  In addition, managed a production support team for a major retail and catalog client.

Programmer
Designed, coded, tested, and promoted enhancements for two client's Distribution Control System implementations.  The enhancements were focused on the Order to Cash and Distribution processes.

about:
As a dynamic and results-oriented experienced Manager within EY’s People Consulting practice, I specialize in strategic Change Management. Grounded in a strong belief in the transformative power of empathy, I develop people-centric change solutions to enable seamless transitions within organizations. My approach to Change Management prioritizes the streamlining of activities while cultivating a culture of adaptability and resilience.

Before joining Consulting, I gained experience as a Sourcing Specialist, Recruiting Coordinator, and Onboarding Specialist across diverse industries, refining my ability to understand and address the evolving needs of both organizations and individuals.

experience.description:
Helping clients implement large scale business transformations by supporting, empowering, and driving sustainable behavior changes. My purpose is to create an exceptional people experience by developing creative and innovative strategies that are both meaningful and helpful for employees and businesses. 

Working primarily on complex cross-functional global programs with Fortune 300 organizations, I’ve had the opportunity to:

• Lead the development of strategy, materials, and delivery of change management activities 
• Own and drive change management efforts on multiple workstreams and act as the primary connector across programs
• Handle fast-moving, sensitive situations with an employee-first mindset and mentor / guide teams
• Act as a trusted client advisor and partner closely with executive leadership to understand vision, measures of success, and provide them with the tools and knowledge needed to drive the change 

Specialties: Stakeholder Analysis & Engagement, Leadership Alignment, Strategic Communications, Training Strategy, Training Creation, Training Delivery, Business Readiness Assessments

Our practical experiences combined with our candor and insights help drive exceptional business results for our clients. 

As an independent member of Baker Tilly International, the world's eighth largest network of accounting firms, we bring you access to market-specific knowledge in more than 133 countries.

Our goal has always been to help candidates find rewarding positions that match their skills and interests, and to provide timely, flexible staffing solutions to help employers find the best candidates.  As a subsidiary of Baker Tilly Virchow Krause, LLP (Baker Tilly), one of the 20 largest accounting and advisory firms in the US, we have access to unique opportunities not available elsewhere.

Hi, I'm Collin, thanks for coming to my page! I'm a Business Consultant for the FSO/Chicago at Ernst & Young. headline: Partner, Talent, EY |  Author ‘The Curious Advantage’ & Podcast Host  |  Senior Fellow
about:
Simon is Global Learning & Development Leader at EY and international best-selling author of the ‘The Curious Advantage’. Previously he was Chief Learning Officer at Novartis.

He is a commercially-minded learning leader with experience across a range of the World's leading organisations.   Having co-founded Brightwave, one of the UK's leading e-Learning companies, Simon moved to Accenture to consult for companies including BT, BP, Microsoft and Canon.  He then focused on the Banking industry, working with Barclays, HSBC and RBS.  Following a series of projects with Lloyds, Simon moved over to deliver the Academy strategy he had designed.  This role then developed into creating the business case for, and then leading the Bank-wide learning transformation.

In 2020 Simon was awarded the Chief Learning Officer, Gold Strategy Award for his and his team's work at Novartis, building on his Silver Strategy Award in 2012 for his work at Lloyds Banking Group.  In 2021 Novartis was recognised as the #3 company in the world for Talent Development in the ATD BEST Awards, as well as receiving multiple other awards and accolades.

In 2013 Simon moved to Novartis global HQ in Switzerland, to set up the Learning Team in the Capability Building Academy, responsible for enhancing effectiveness of learning for the global pharma salesforce and commercial business. In 2016 he moved to the Drug Development world and created the cross-divisional 'Global Development University', before progressing in September 2017 to take over the Novartis-wide Learning CoE and Novartis Universities, and also define the strategy for Digital Capability Building. 

Simon also hosts, with his co-authors, the popular podcast The Curious Advantage, which is in the top 5% of podcasts globally, and has been in the Apple Management Podcasts Top 5 in 20 countries.  He is a regular keynote speaker at events internationally.

Member of World Economic Forum Chief Learning Officer Community, the Gartner L&D Leadership Board, & supporting the next generation of learning and EdTech companies as an angel investor.

Specialties: Learning, strategy, digital, change, transformation, leadership, programme management, innovation

headline: Technology Risk Senior Manager at EY
topSkills: Internal Controls • Risk Assurance • Cross-functional Team Leadership • Continuous Improvement • Auditing
about:
I am a bold and ambitious Technology Risk Senior Manager who helps organizations embrace the rapidly changing risk landscape. I bring valuable insights and technical expertise that empower businesses to proactively manage risks, respond to uncertainty, and create long-term value.

My journey in the field of technology risk has equipped me with a deep understanding of the challenges and opportunities that businesses face in today's digital age. 

Throughout my career, I have enjoyed leading cross-functional teams in evaluating compliance, data quality, and the adequacy of controls, collaborating with internal and external stakeholders, and driving continuous improvement initiatives.

I am passionate about continuous learning, helping others, and making a positive impact in the world. 

Let's connect and explore how we can collaborate to address your technology risk challenges and drive sustainable growth.

Specialties: 
System and Organization Controls (SOC) Reporting (SOC 1, SOC 2, SOC 3), Internal Control Over Financial Reporting (ICFR), Internal Controls, IT Audit / IT Internal Audit / Financial Audit IT, IT Internal Control Assessment, Sarbanes-Oxley (SOX) Compliance, IT Risk Management and Assurance, Information Security, Cybersecurity, Data Protection, Data Privacy, Process Improvements, Control Assessment and Gap Remediation, Cloud Computing, Software-as-a-Service (SaaS).

headline: Insurance Business Architect | Business Transformation Consultant
topSkills: Property & Casualty Insurance • Insurance • Underwriting • Customer Relations
about:
As a consultant at a Big Four accounting firm focusing on large software transformations in the insurance industry, I advise national carriers how to improve their business processes to drive results – and increase profits. I enjoy serving as a counselor and mentor to three colleagues and my leadership style is focused on inclusion and fostering a collaborative and productive work environment.

I earned my MBA from the University of Chicago Booth School of Business and graduated with concentrations in Strategic Management; Econometrics and Statistics; Finance; Marketing Management and Entrepreneurship. Leveraging the skills I honed during my time at Booth, including building high-performing teams, managing complex projects and making strategic decisions, I am able to effectively serve as a trusted advisor to my clients.
  
I transitioned into my current corporate advisory role after earning the respect of my business partners and peers as a commercial underwriter at an international insurance company. Starting at the company in an entry-level position, I worked my way up to Senior Account Executive by focusing on the needs of my clients, which allowed me to consistently exceed my premium goals and increase profits for the company.

Over 20 years of industry experience combined with my educational background allows me to bring credible counsel and innovative, sustainable and cost-effective solutions to any project.

headline: Sustainability | Biodiversity | CSRD | Climate Migration
about:
My experience coming from developing nations highlights my constant concern about social aspects, mainly as vulnerable regions are the most environmentally affected. That is why in order to polish my sustainable skills, I chose to come to Sweden, where I pursued my Master's Degree in Sustainable Development at Uppsala University & SLU. 

My Thesis Research concerned 1) identifying environmental drivers leading to climate migration in Guatemala and 2) prioritizing loss and damage funds for these drivers management costs. Climate migration and human mobility are my absolute favorite areas in the interconnection between social and environmental issues.

I believe my duty is to multiply the privileges I have had and inspire people who would otherwise be beyond my reach. I do this through my work (I work at EY as a Sustainability Senior Consultant), volunteering projects (more on that in the volunteering section below), and the lifestyle I choose to have (if interested in that, my inbox is opened for a chat!). 

E-mail: rebeca.montes@se.ey.com | rebeca.ferreira.montes@gmail.com
